_why: ADR 0094's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
Two defects, one shape: a check that computed the right number and
compared it to the wrong thing.
check_doc_paths_resolve.py went red because the pass that fixed the
clone-URL disagreement wrote the explanation into START_HERE.md,
backticking three repository slugs. `Terrium-sim/terrium.git` has the
shape of a repo-relative path and is not one. A guard born from a
wrong path typed while fixing paths was taken down by prose typed
while fixing prose.
test_archive_counts_are_current.py computed root_count() and
deliberately declined to assert it, guarding the dated claim on line
43 of DOCUMENTATION_INDEX.md while the undated live one on line 3
said the root holds 81 markdown files. It holds 41.
P4 is the row that mattered most: it attacks the FIX rather than the
code, by making the remote classifier match everything. Under the
original floor -- which counted tokens seen, not tokens verified --
that passes green having checked nothing. P5 is that earlier floor,
kept as a row so the reason the floor moved stays reproducible.
A9 is the accident. root_count() globbed dotfiles and counted
`.aider.chat.history.md`, which is in .gitignore and untracked, so no
clone has ever contained it. The prose numbers came from a shell
glob, which skips dotfiles. The two had been measuring different sets
since the function was written, and it was invisible for exactly as
long as nothing compared them.
Run:  python3 scripts/mutate.py --set docs/mutations/adr-0094-the-guard-the-fix-broke.json
test: python3 -m pytest Tests/test_doc_paths_resolve.py Tests/test_archive_counts_are_current.py Tests/test_clone_instructions_agree.py -q -p no:cacheprovider

mutations.description: the test the .git exemption is handed off to no longer reads clone commands
mutations._note: The exemption is a delegation, not a skip. If the delegate stops checking, nothing checks the clone URLs and the guard must say so rather than continuing to wave three tokens through.

mutations.description: the handoff check accepts a delegate that never mentions .git
mutations._note: Two conditions, because a test could keep the words `git clone` while losing the URL matching that makes the delegation real.
mutations.find:
if ".git" not in text:
        return f"{HANDOFF} no longer matches `.git` URLs"

mutations.description: the remote classifier matches nothing, so the exemption disappears
mutations._note: Removing the exemption must not pass quietly either -- the three slugs go straight back to being reported as missing files, which is the defect this ADR opens with.

mutations.description: the remote classifier matches EVERYTHING, delegating every token
mutations._note: The vacuity attack. Every path-shaped token becomes somebody else's problem and zero are verified. Caught only because the floor counts what was checked.

mutations.description: the floor counts tokens seen rather than tokens verified, and everything is delegated
mutations._note: This is the version that shipped first, and the row that decided the design. The hole needs two things at once -- a floor counting tokens seen, and a classifier swallowing them -- and mutate.py applies one edit per row. A two-part row was written first; the harness has no key for it, so it would have applied half, reported on a mutation that never happened, and been believed. The property is asserted instead, by test_delegating_everything_trips_the_floor, which supplies the swallowing classifier itself. So this row mutates only the floor and the test provides the other half.

mutations.description: the original defect replayed: the index says the root holds 81
mutations._note: The verbatim historical text. A guard that cannot fail on the thing it was written for is decoration.

mutations.description: the live sentence is deleted rather than corrected
mutations._note: Deleting the claim satisfies a naive count check by removing what it counts. Both the presence test and the value test have to fire.
mutations.find: The repository root holds 41 markdown files.

mutations.description: the live sentence is relabelled as a dated one
mutations._note: The subtler escape: rewrite `holds 41` as `held 41 as of 2026-08-16` and the live claim is gone while the file still looks careful. Dating a number is the right move for a finished migration and the wrong move for a directory that changes.
mutations.find: The repository root holds 41 markdown files.
mutations.replace: The root held 41 markdown files as of 2026-08-16.

mutations.description: root_count() goes back to globbing dotfiles
mutations._note: Found by accident: the new assertion failed on its first real run, 41 against 42, because the glob counted a gitignored aider scratch file. Kept as a row because the off-by-one was undetectable until something compared the number to a document.

mutations.description: the dated claim stops needing a date
mutations._note:
The other half of the tense rule. Without this, `as of YYYY-MM-DD` could be dropped from the migration sentence and an undated historical number would read as current -- which is the failure check_investor_claims.py exists to draw.
    The find string carries its error message as context. The bare regex now appears twice -- once in the original assertion, once in the presence test added beside it -- and the harness returned INDETERMINATE rather than guessing which. That is the behaviour worth having: a coin-flip between two call sites would have produced a confident verdict about an unknown edit.
mutations.find:
markdown files to \d+ as of \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", text), (
        "DOCUMENTATION_INDEX.md states what the root count became without "
mutations.replace:
markdown files to \d+ ON \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", text), (
        "DOCUMENTATION_INDEX.md states what the root count became without "
